name: Presence Lab
tagline: Be heard in the rooms that matter
about: Presence Lab sharpens how you come across in senior meetings — strips hedging from your messages, preps your one point for the leadership meeting, rehearses recovering the floor when you're talked over and analyses transcripts of you for filler and waffle.
persona: You are an executive communication coach for rising leaders: direct, specific, allergic to filler; you focus on behaviours that can change this week, not on personality.

onboarding.title: Executive presence is a set of habits
onboarding.subtitle: Tell us where you struggle; every drill targets it.

profile.label: Where you struggle
options: I go quiet in senior rooms

profile.label: The rooms you're in
profile.placeholder: weekly leadership meeting, QBRs with clients

tools.title: De-hedge my message
tools.subtitle: Cut the 'just', 'sort of', 'I think maybe'

inputs.label: Paste what you're about to send or say
inputs.placeholder: I just wanted to check if maybe we could possibly…

tools.prompt: Rewrite this to remove hedging and filler while staying {keep}: {draft}. Sections: a quote with the rewritten version; a table (Original phrase | Why it weakens | Replacement) for every hedge found; kv (Words before → after, Asks made explicit); and a callout on the one habit in this draft that matches the profile's stated struggles.

tools.title: My one point
tools.subtitle: Make it in 30 seconds

inputs.label: The meeting and what you want to land
inputs.placeholder: leadership meeting; I want them to stop adding scope to the migration

tools.prompt: Prepare a {seconds} contribution for: {context}. Sections: a quote with the exact words (claim first, one piece of evidence, one ask); bullets on when in the meeting to say it and how to get the floor; a table (Pushback | 10-second reply) with 3 rows; and a callout on the signal that it's time to stop talking.

tools.title: I got talked over
tools.subtitle: Recover the floor gracefully

inputs.label: What happened
inputs.placeholder: VP cut me off mid-sentence, moved on, my idea was later credited to him

tools.prompt: Situation: {what}. The user wants tactics for: {when}. Sections: a table (Tactic | Words to use | Risk) with 5 tactics matched to the profile's level; a quote with the single best line for this case; steps for a follow-up that reclaims the idea without accusing anyone; and a callout on when this is a pattern worth raising with a manager or sponsor.

tools.title: Analyse my transcript
tools.subtitle: Paste a transcript of you speaking

inputs.label: Transcript of you speaking
inputs.placeholder: So, um, I think what we're seeing is, like…

tools.prompt: Analyse this transcript of the user speaking: {transcript}. Sections: kv (Filler words per minute est., Hedges, Average sentence length, Time to first point, Questions vs statements); a table (Habit | Example from the transcript | Replacement) with the top 5 habits; a quote restating the same content the way a confident senior leader would say it in under half the words; and steps for a one-week drill on the single biggest habit.

tools.title: Introduce myself upward
tools.subtitle: Meeting a senior leader for the first time

inputs.label: Who you're meeting and why
inputs.placeholder: new CFO, 20-minute intro, I lead data platform

tools.prompt: Prepare the user to meet {who}, wanting: {want}. Sections: a quote with a 30-second self-introduction (role, what you own, one result, what you'd like from them); bullets of 5 questions to ask that show judgement; a table (They'll probably ask | Crisp answer) with 4 rows; and a callout on what to send afterwards and within how many hours.
